packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP01 vv001-011
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP01
Unit: 5:1–11 (11 verses)
Surah tag: Medinan by the traditional list
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

O believers, fulfill the contracts. Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock except what is recited to you, not making hunting lawful while you are in iḥrām. God judges what He wills. O believers, do not violate God’s rites, nor the sacred month, nor the sacrificial offerings, nor the garlands, nor those repairing to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and pleasure. When you have left iḥrām, hunt. Do not let hatred of a people who barred you from the Sacred Mosque provoke you to transgress. Cooperate in birr and taqwā; do not cooperate in sin and aggression. Fear God. Forbidden to you: carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, what has been dedicated to other than God, the strangled, the beaten-to-death, the fallen, the gored, what beasts have eaten except what you purify, what is slaughtered on stone altars, and that you divide by arrows — that is fisq. Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your dīn; do not fear them, fear Me. Today I have perfected your dīn for you, completed My favor on you, and approved islām as a dīn for you. Whoever is forced by hunger, not inclining to sin: God is forgiving, merciful. They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: the good things are lawful, and what you have taught of hunting animals, teaching them as God taught you. Eat of what they catch for you and mention God’s name over it. This day the good things are lawful; the food of those given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them; and the chaste women of the believers and the chaste women of those given the Book before you, when you give them their wages, seeking chastity not unchastity or secret lovers. Whoever denies īmān, his work is fruitless; in the hereafter he is of the losers. O believers, when you stand for prayer, wash your faces and your hands to the elbows, wipe your heads, wash your feet to the ankles. If you are junub, purify. If ill or on a journey or from the privy or you have touched women and find no water: clean earth, wipe faces and hands. God does not want to place hardship on you; He wants to purify you and complete His favor. Remember God’s favor and the covenant He bound you with when you said we hear and we obey. O believers, be qawwāmīn for God, witnesses with qisṭ. Do not let hatred of a people provoke you not to be just. Be just; that is nearer to taqwā. God promised those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt forgiveness and a great reward.
2–3. Investigation
5:1–2 contracts; iḥrām hunting; do not let hatred transgress

First word of the surah after the address: fulfill the ʿuqūd. Livestock lawful except what will be recited; hunting not while ḥurum. Do not violate rites, sacred month, hady, garlands, or those heading to the Sacred House. After iḥrām, hunt. Hatred of a people who barred you from the Mosque is not a license to ʿudwān. Cooperate in birr and taqwā; not in ithm and ʿudwān. The barred-from-the-Mosque memory is the Ḥudaybiya / Quraysh file in the tradition. Level 1 is the rule: prior obstruction does not authorize present transgression.
5:3 the ban-list and “today I perfected”

Carrion, blood, swine, dedicated-to-other-than-God: already 2:173 / 16:115. New in this list: strangled, beaten, fallen, gored, beasts’ leftovers unless you purify, stone-altar slaughter, dividing by azlām (arrows). That last is named fisq. Then the despair-sentence: those who disbelieve have despaired of your dīn; do not fear them, fear Me. Then: al-yawma akmaltu lakum dīnakum wa-atmamtu ʿalaykum niʿmatī wa-raḍītu lakumu l-islāma dīnan. Forced by hunger, not inclining to sin: forgiven.

“Today I perfected the dīn” is one of the heaviest dating-verses in the tradition (Farewell Pilgrimage). Level 1 is the claim of completion and of islām approved as dīn — same word that 3:19 and 3:85 already used. Hunger-exception keeps the ban-list from becoming a death sentence.

QB-0107: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Lev 11 / Deut 14 on carrion, blood, swine. ADDITION of the death-mode list (strangled, beaten, fallen, gored) and of stone-altar / arrow-lots. NT trajectory is Mark 7 / Acts 10 / 15 (food laws relaxed for the nations). Three architectures again: Torah species-and-blood, Gospel/apostolic relaxation, this verse’s completed list plus hunger-exception.
5:4 trained hunters
Good things lawful. What you have trained of hunting animals, as God taught you: eat what they catch for you; name God over it. A permission-structure for trained predators, fenced by tasmiya.
5:5 food of the Book-people; their chaste women

This day the good things are lawful. The food of those given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. Chaste women of the believers and chaste women of those given the Book before you — wages paid, chastity not unchastity or secret lovers. Whoever denies īmān: work fruitless; loser in the hereafter.

Ṭaʿām of the People of the Book is received in tafsir as their slaughtered meat, not every plate. Level 1 is “their food is lawful for you and yours for them” — a two-way table-fellowship sentence. It sits after 3:93 (bring the Torah; Jacob’s self-ban) and after 2:173’s short ban-list.

Marriage: muḥṣanāt of the Book-people are named lawful in a way 2:221 (do not marry mushrikāt until they believe) is not simply repeated. Later fiqh restricts “Book” and “chaste.” Level 1 is the permission plus the chastity-and-wage fence plus the īmān-denial closer.

QB-0108: CONTRAST with Torah’s tight food-and-marriage fence toward the nations (Deut 7; Ezra 9–10). PARTIAL AGREEMENT that a named outsider-group can sit at the table and enter the house under conditions. Acts 15 keeps blood and strangled in the apostolic memo; 5:3 also keeps them. 5:5 then opens Book-people food anyway. The two verses have to live together.
5:6–7 wuḍūʾ and tayammum restated; hear-and-obey covenant

Stand for prayer: wash faces, hands to elbows, wipe heads, wash feet to ankles. Junub: purify. No water: earth, wipe faces and hands. Same substitute as 4:43, now with a fuller wash-sequence. God wants to purify and complete the favor — the completion-word from 5:3 echoed. Remember the covenant: we hear and we obey.
5:8–11 justice even toward those you hate; promise

Qawwāmīn for God, witnesses with qisṭ. Do not let hatred of a people provoke you not to be just. Be just; that is nearer to taqwā. Repeats 4:135 and 5:2’s hatred-clause, now aimed at justice rather than at ʿudwān. Promise: believers who do ṣāliḥāt get forgiveness and a great reward. Those who disbelieve and call the signs a lie: companions of Jahīm.
4–9. IDs
QB
Item
Call

PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Lev 11 blood/swine; NT relaxes; this list adds death-modes and lots
Book-people food and chaste women lawful
CONTRAST with Deut 7 / Ezra fence; PARTIAL AGREEMENT with a conditioned opening

21–22. Summary and next

Al-Māʾida opens on contracts, a completed dīn-claim, a longer food list, and a two-way table with the People of the Book plus marriage to their chaste women. Hatred is named twice as a justice-test. Next: 5:12–26 (covenant with Banī Isrāʾīl; twelve chiefs; enter the holy land; two men).

packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP02 vv012-026
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP02
Unit: 5:12–26 (15 verses)
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

God took the covenant of the Children of Israel and We raised from them twelve chiefs. God said: I am with you. If you establish prayer, give zakāt, believe in My messengers and support them, and lend God a good loan, I will cover your evils and admit you to Gardens. Whoever disbelieves after that has strayed from the even way. For their breaking the covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They displace words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of. You will not cease to find treachery from them except a few. Pardon and overlook. From those who say we are Christians We took their covenant; they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of; We stirred among them enmity and hatred to the Day of Rising. God will inform them of what they used to do. People of the Book: Our messenger has come to you making clear much of what you were hiding of the Book and passing over much. There has come to you from God a light and a clear Book. By it God guides those who follow His pleasure to the ways of peace. Those who say God is the Messiah son of Mary have disbelieved. Who can do anything against God if He wanted to destroy the Messiah son of Mary and his mother and whoever is in the earth? Those who say God is a third of three have disbelieved. There is no god but one God. The Messiah son of Mary is only a messenger; messengers have passed before him; his mother was a ṣiddīqa; they both ate food. People of the Book, do not go beyond bounds in your dīn other than the truth.

Cut note: 5:20–26 is the land-refusal panel and belongs in this packet. 5:17–19 Messiah-claims sit between the covenant-break and the land story; they are included so the messenger-to-Book-people block is not split from its immediate Christology.
Wait — land panel is 5:20–26. Restate that block

When Moses said to his people: O my people, remember God’s favor on you when He made prophets among you and made you kings and gave you what He had not given any of the worlds. O my people, enter the holy land which God has written for you; do not turn on your backs and return as losers. They said: O Moses, in it is a people of jabbarīn; we will not enter it until they go out of it; if they go out we will enter. Two men of those who fear, whom God had favored, said: enter upon them the gate; if you enter it you will be overcomers; rely on God if you are believers. They said: we will never enter it as long as they are in it. You and your Lord go and fight; we are sitting here. He said: my Lord, I control only myself and my brother; distinguish between us and the fāsiq people. He said: it is forbidden to them forty years; they will wander in the earth. Do not grieve over the fāsiq people.
2–3. Investigation
5:12–14 two covenants; twelve chiefs; forgotten portion

Israel’s covenant: twelve naqībs; God is with you if you pray, give zakāt, believe in My messengers and support them, and lend a good loan. After-kufr is named as leaving the sawāʾ al-sabīl. For breaking it: curse, hard hearts, yuharrifūna l-kalima ʿan mawāḍiʿihi, and they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. Treachery except a few; pardon them. Those who say we are Naṣārā: covenant taken; they too forgot a portion; enmity and hatred stirred among them to the Rising.

Tahrīf here is again displacement of words plus forgetting a portion — not a global-rewritten-file theorem. The Christian file is “forgot a portion” plus intra-Christian enmity, not the same hard-hearts sentence as Israel in 5:13.

Twelve chiefs: QB-0109 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Num 13’s twelve spies (one per tribe) and with the twelve tribal nesi’im. Tafsir also hears the ʿAqaba twelve. Level 1 is twelve naqībs raised from Israel in a covenant scene.
5:15–16 messenger making clear what was hidden

Our messenger has come making clear much of what you hid of the Book and passing over much. A light and a clear Book from God. He guides followers of His pleasure to ways of peace, out of darknesses to light. Hiding + passing-over: the Quran claims to disclose some concealed material and to skip some. That is a theory of selective disclosure, not of total reprint.
5:17–18 God is the Messiah / third of three

Those who say God is the Messiah son of Mary have disbelieved. Who can stop God if He wanted to destroy the Messiah and his mother and everyone on earth? Those who say God is a third of three have disbelieved. No god but one. Desist or a painful punishment. Will they not turn? The Messiah is only a messenger; messengers have passed before him; his mother was a ṣiddīqa; they both ate food.

Eating food is the Quran’s anti-divinity test in this verse: bodies that eat are not God. 4:171 said do not say three; 5:17–18 names the two slogans (God is the Messiah; God is a third of three) and calls both kufr.
QB-0110 CONTRAST with John 1 / 10 / 20 and Nicene “true God from true God.” The food-test is this text’s own. Mary as ṣiddīqa blocks a goddess-pair reading of 5:116 in advance.
5:20–26 enter the land written for you

Moses: remember favor — prophets among you, made kings, given what no world was given. Enter the holy land God has written for you; do not turn back. They: a people of jabbarīn; we will not enter until they leave. Two men of those who fear, God-favored: enter the gate; you will overcome; rely on God. They: we will never enter while they are in it. You and your Lord go fight; we sit. Moses: I control only myself and my brother; distinguish us from the fāsiq people. Forbidden forty years; they wander the earth. Do not grieve.

QB-0111 AGREEMENT of plot with Num 13–14 / Deut 1:19–46: spies / refusal / two faithful voices / “we will not go up” / forty years in the wilderness. DIFFERENCE: the Quran does not name the land as Canaan, does not name the two men (tafsir: Joshua and Caleb), does not stage the giant-grape cluster, and has the people say “you and your Lord go fight.” Made-kings is this telling’s own (HB kingship is later). “Written for you” is a land-claim sentence; this project records it without adjudicating modern politics.
4–9. IDs

Two covenants, both charged with forgetting a portion. The messenger discloses some hidden material and skips some. “God is the Messiah” and “third of three” are named kufr; the Messiah and his mother ate food. The land story is Numbers 13–14 with the names stripped and “you and your Lord go fight” added. Next: 5:27–40 (Adam’s two sons; the killing; the burying-raven; ḥirāba).

packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP03 vv027-040
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP03
Unit: 5:27–40 (14 verses)
Pair with: Exam_Cain_Abel_5_27-32.docx
Date: 11 September 2026
Describes ḥudūd clauses. Not a sentencing manual.
1. Overview

Recite the story of Adam’s two sons in truth. Two offerings; accepted from one. I will kill you. God accepts only from the muttaqīn. I will not stretch my hand; I want you to bear both sins. His nafs prompted him; he killed him; he became a loser. A crow taught him to hide the sawʾa; he regretted. Because of that We wrote on Israel: killing a soul not for a soul or for fasād in the land is as if killing all people; giving it life is as if giving life to all. Messengers came with bayyināt; many after that commit excess in the land. The repayment of those who wage war on God and His messenger and strive for fasād in the land: that they be killed, or crucified, or their hands and feet be cut from opposite sides, or they be banished from the land. That is disgrace in this world; in the hereafter a great punishment — except those who repent before you have power over them. Know that God is forgiving, merciful. O believers, fear God and seek the means to Him and strive in His way that you may succeed. Those who disbelieve, if they had what is in the earth all together and the like of it with it to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Rising, it would not be accepted; they have a painful punishment. They want to go out of the Fire; they are not going out; they have an enduring punishment. The male and female thief: cut their hands as a repayment for what they earned, a nakāl from God. God is mighty, wise. Whoever repents after his ẓulm and puts things right: God turns to him. Do you not know that to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills.
2–3. Investigation
5:27–32 two sons — pointer

Full scene-by-scene against Genesis 4 and Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 is in Exam_Cain_Abel_5_27-32.docx (QB-0112–0115; QDISC-0196–0198). This packet does not reprint that table. What this packet needs from 5:32 is the hinge into 5:33: the fasād-in-the-land exception is the door the next verse walks through.
5:33–34 ḥirāba

Those who yuḥāribūna Allāha wa-rasūlahu and yasʿawna fī l-arḍi fasādan: killed, or crucified, or hands and feet from opposite sides, or banished from the land. World-disgrace; hereafter a great punishment. Except who repent before you have power over them.

Four named repayments, or-clauses. Traditional fiqh treats this as highway robbery / armed terror against the public order (ḥirāba), and then argues which act maps to which penalty. That mapping is Level 4. Level 1 is the four-or list plus a repentance window that closes once “you have power over them.”
Ṣalb here is the same root as 4:157’s “they did not crucify him.” Different file: a ḥadd option, not the Jesus scene. Do not merge the two ṣ-l-b verses.

QB-0116: POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP with Torah extreme-penalty lists for public violence (Exod 22:2 night-thief; Num 35; Deut 13 / 17 public evil) and with Roman crucifixion as a public-order death. The four-option menu is this verse’s own. This packet describes the menu. It does not apply it.
5:35–37 seek the means; ransom will not work

Fear God; seek the wasīla to Him; strive in His way. If the disbelievers had the earth twice over as ransom from the Rising-punishment it would not be accepted. They want out of the Fire; they are not coming out.
5:38–40 male and female thief

Al-sāriqu wa-l-sāriqatu fa-iqṭaʿū aydiyahumā — cut their hands — repayment for what they earned, a nakāl from God. Whoever repents after his ẓulm and puts things right: God turns to him. Kingdom is God’s; He punishes and forgives whom He wills.

Level 1 names male and female together and names cutting of hands as repayment and deterrent. Nisāb, which hand, first offense, famine exceptions: all later fiqh. 12:31 uses the same root for the women cutting their hands at Joseph — different scene, same verb family. 5:38 is a ḥadd verse. Describe it; do not write a procedure.

QB-0117: CONTRAST with Torah theft law, which is restitution-centered (Exod 22:1–4: pay back multiple; if nothing, sold for the theft). Hand-cutting as the named repayment is this verse’s own architecture. Later rabbinic and Christian legal histories go other ways.

packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP04 vv041-050
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP04
Unit: 5:41–50 (10 verses)
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

O messenger, do not grieve over those who rush into kufr from those who say we believe with their mouths while their hearts do not believe, and from those who are Jews, listeners to the lie, listeners for another people who have not come to you. They displace words from their places. They say if you are given this take it, and if you are not given it beware. Whom God wants to trial you will not own for him anything from God. Those are the ones whose hearts God did not want to purify; disgrace in this world and a great punishment in the hereafter. Listeners to the lie, eaters of the suḥt. If they come to you, judge between them or turn from them. If you turn from them they will not harm you at all. If you judge, judge between them with qisṭ. God loves the just. How do they make you judge when they have the Torah in which is God’s judgment, then they turn away after that? Those are not believers. We sent down the Torah; in it is guidance and light. The prophets who submitted judged the Jews by it, and the rabbāniyyūn and the aḥbār, with what they were given to keep of God’s Book and they were witnesses over it. Do not fear people; fear Me. Do not sell My signs for a small price. Whoever does not judge by what God sent down — those are the kāfirūn. We wrote on them in it: a nafs for a nafs, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth; wounds qiṣāṣ. Whoever gives it as ṣadaqa, it is an expiation for him. Whoever does not judge by what God sent down — those are the ẓālimūn. We sent in their tracks Jesus son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah; We gave him the Injīl; in it is guidance and light, confirming what was before him of the Torah, a guidance and an admonition for the muttaqīn. Let the people of the Injīl judge by what God sent down in it. Whoever does not judge by what God sent down — those are the fāsiqūn. We sent down to you the Book with truth, confirming what is before it of the Book and muhayminan over it. So judge between them by what God sent down and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you. For each of you We made a shirʿa and a minhāj. If God had willed He would have made you one ummah, but to test you in what He gave you. Race to the good things. To God is your return all together; He will tell you about what you used to differ in. Judge between them by what God sent down and do not follow their desires. Beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what God sent down to you. If they turn away, know that God wants to hit them for some of their sins. Many of the people are fāsiqūn. Is it the judgment of Jāhiliyya they want? Who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain?
2–3. Investigation
5:41–43 shopping for a judgment

Two groups rush into kufr: mouth-believers whose hearts do not, and some Jews who listen to the lie for another people who have not come to you. They displace words. They say: if you are given this (ruling), take it; if not, beware. Listeners to the lie, eaters of suḥt (ill-gotten). The messenger may judge between them or turn away; if he judges, with qisṭ. How do they appoint you judge when they have the Torah in which is God’s ḥukm — then they turn away? Those are not believers.

Level 1: a forum-shopping charge. The Torah is named as already containing God’s judgment. Coming to this messenger and then walking away if the answer is inconvenient is named as unbelief. Traditional asbāb: a ḥadd / adultery / blood-money case they hoped he would lighten. TRADITION for the case-name. Level 1 is the shop-and-leave pattern plus the Torah-already-has-it sentence.
5:44 Torah: guidance and light; prophets and rabbis judged by it

We sent down the Torah; in it is hudā and nūr. The prophets who were muslims judged the Jews by it; so did the rabbāniyyūn and aḥbār, with what they were entrusted of God’s Book; they were witnesses over it. Do not fear people; do not sell the signs. Whoever does not judge by what God sent down: those are the kāfirūn.

This is the strongest “the Torah in their hands is still a judging-book” verse so far. The keepers are named: prophets, rabbis, scholars. QCA-0004 thickens: confirmation plus present-tense judging-duty. Tahrīf in 5:41 is displacement in the shopped case, sitting next to a verse that still calls the Torah guidance and light.
5:45 nafs for nafs; eye for eye

We wrote on them in it: a soul for a soul, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth; wounds qiṣāṣ. Whoever gives it as charity, it is kaffāra for him. Whoever does not judge by what God sent down: those are the ẓālimūn.

QB-0118 AGREEMENT with Exod 21:23–25 / Lev 24:19–20 / Deut 19:21 lex talionis. The Quran adds that remitting it as ṣadaqa is an expiation — a mercy-clause not in those three Torah sentences (though later Jewish law knows compounding). 2:178 already had qiṣāṣ with a brother-pardon. 5:45 locates the same architecture inside “We wrote it on them in the Torah.”
5:46–47 Jesus and the Injīl

We sent in their tracks Jesus son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah. We gave him the Injīl; in it is guidance and light, confirming the Torah, a guidance and admonition for the muttaqīn. Let the people of the Injīl judge by what God sent down in it. Whoever does not judge by what God sent down: those are the fāsiqūn.

Three labels in three verses for not judging by what God sent down: kāfirūn (44), ẓālimūn (45), fāsiqūn (47). Do not collapse them too fast; the tradition argues whether they name three groups or three aspects. Level 1 is three different nouns on the same “who does not judge by mā anzala llāh” frame.

The people of the Injīl are told to judge by what is in it. That is a present-tense duty aimed at them, parallel to 5:44’s Torah-duty. QCA-0004 / QI-0003: the prior books are not treated here as void paper.
5:48 muhaymin; a law and a way for each

We sent down to you the Book with truth, confirming what is before it of the Book and muhayminan ʿalayhi. Judge between them by what God sent down; do not follow their desires. For each of you We made a shirʿa and a minhāj. If God had willed He would have made you one ummah; He tests you in what He gave you. Race to the khayrāt. Return is to God; He will tell you about what you differed in.

Muhaymin: watcher / trustee / overseer over the prior Book. Not “erases” in this sentence. Confirming + overseeing + then “for each a law and a way” + “if He willed, one ummah.” That last cluster is why this verse is the project’s best single statement of plurality-under-test. It sits in the same surah as 3:19 / 3:85 / 5:3’s perfected-dīn. QI-0004 remains OPEN: these sentences all stand.

QB-0119 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Acts 15 / Rom 2 plurality-of-jurisdiction motifs, and with the Torah’s own “one law for the native and the sojourner” being a different theory (one law, not each-a-law). The Quran here names multiple tracks and a race to the good, with God adjudicating the difference at the return.
5:49–50 do not follow their desires; Jāhiliyya judgment

Judge by what God sent down. Beware they tempt you off some of it. If they turn away, God wants to hit them for some sin. Is it Jāhiliyya’s judgment they want? Who is better than God in judgment for a people who know?

packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP05 vv051-066
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP05
Unit: 5:51–66 (16 verses)
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

O believers, do not take the Jews and the Christians as awliyāʾ; they are awliyāʾ of one another. Whoever of you turns to them is of them. God does not guide the ẓālim people. You see those in whose hearts is a disease racing toward them, saying we fear a turn of fortune. God may bring fatḥ or a command from Him; then they will become regretful of what they hid in themselves. Those who believe will say: are these the ones who swore by God the strongest of their oaths that they were with you? Their works have failed; they have become losers. O believers, whoever of you turns back from his dīn: God will bring a people He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, hard toward the disbelievers, striving in God’s way, not fearing the blame of a blamer. That is God’s bounty; He gives it to whom He wills. Your walī is only God and His messenger and those who believe — who establish prayer and give zakāt and they bow. Whoever turns to God and His messenger and those who believe: the ḥizb of God are the overcomers. O believers, do not take as awliyāʾ those who take your dīn in mockery and play from those given the Book before you and the disbelievers. Fear God if you are believers. When you call to prayer they take it in mockery and play. That is because they are a people who do not understand. Say: People of the Book, do you resent us except that we believe in God and what was sent down to us and what was sent down before, and that most of you are fāsiqūn? Say: shall I tell you of worse than that as a repayment with God? Those whom God cursed and was angry with, and made of them apes and pigs, and the ʿabd of ṭāghūt. Those are worse in place and further astray from the even way. When they come to you they say we believe; they have entered with kufr and they have left with it. God knows best what they were hiding. You see many of them racing into sin and aggression and eating the suḥt. How evil is what they were doing. If the rabbāniyyūn and the aḥbār had forbidden them from their sinful speech and their eating of suḥt, how evil is what they were crafting. The Jews said God’s hand is chained. Their hands are chained and they are cursed for what they said. Rather His hands are outspread; He spends as He wills. What was sent down to you from your Lord will increase many of them in rebellion and kufr. We have cast among them enmity and hatred to the Day of Rising. Whenever they kindle a fire for war God extinguishes it. They strive for fasād in the land; God does not love those who work fasād. If the People of the Book had believed and feared, We would have covered their evils and admitted them to Gardens of bliss. If they had upheld the Torah and the Injīl and what was sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from under their feet. Among them is a balanced ummah; many of them — how evil is what they do.
2–3. Investigation
5:51–58 awliyāʾ; mockery of the call to prayer

Do not take the Jews and the Christians as awliyāʾ; they are awliyāʾ of one another; whoever turns to them is of them. Walī / awliyāʾ ranges across ally, guardian, patron, intimate protector. This project keeps the range and does not flatten the verse into “no courtesy” or into “no treaties.” The diseased-heart party races toward them fearing a turn of fortune. God may bring fatḥ; then they regret. Swearers that they were with you: their works fail.

Whoever turns back from his dīn: God will bring a people He loves and who love Him — humble to believers, hard to disbelievers, striving, not fearing blame. Your walī is only God, His messenger, and those who believe, who pray and give zakāt and bow. The ḥizb of God are the overcomers. Do not take as awliyāʾ those who take your dīn as mockery and play — from the Book-people and the disbelievers. When you call to prayer they take it as mockery because they do not understand.

5:5 permitted Book-people food and marriage to their chaste women. 5:51 restricts walāya. Both sentences stand in one surah. That is a distinction (table and household vs patronage-alliance), not a cancellation.

QB-0120: POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP with Ezra–Nehemiah’s ban on foreign alliance-marriage and with John 15 / 2 Cor 6 “do not be unequally yoked.” Different fences, same family of problems: how a covenant people treats outside patrons.
5:59–63 resent us for believing both sendings; apes and pigs

Do you resent us only because we believe in God and what was sent down to us and what was sent down before — and that most of you are fāsiqūn? Worse as repayment: those God cursed and was angry with, and made of them apes and pigs, and the servant of ṭāghūt. They enter saying we believe and leave in kufr. Many race into ithm, ʿudwān, eating suḥt. If the rabbis and scholars had forbidden them, how evil is what they crafted.

Apes already appeared at 2:65 (sabbath). Pigs are new in the pair. 7:166 will return the sabbath-apes. Level 1 is a curse-and-transformation sentence aimed at a cursed group, used here as “worse than your resentment.” Do not turn it into a biology claim about living populations.
5:64 God’s hand is chained

The Jews said God’s hand is chained. Their hands are chained and they are cursed for what they said. Rather His two hands are outspread; He spends as He wills. What was sent down to you increases many of them in ṭughyān and kufr. Enmity and hatred among them to the Rising. Whenever they kindle a war-fire God puts it out. They strive for fasād; God does not love the workers of fasād.

QB-0121: POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP with Israel’s complaint-traditions about withheld blessing (and with later caricatures of divine tightness). The Quran treats “God’s hand is chained” as a slander and answers with two outspread hands that spend. Anthropomorphism of two hands is left standing; later kalām will argue mode. Level 1 is the slander plus the outspread-spending answer.
5:65–66 if they had upheld Torah and Injīl

If the People of the Book had believed and feared, We would have covered their evils and admitted them to Gardens. If they had upheld (aqāmū) the Torah and the Injīl and what was sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from under their feet. Among them is an ummah muqtaṣida; many of them — how evil is what they do.

Upholding both books plus “what was sent down to them from their Lord” (this sending, in context) is named as the condition of eating from above and below — a plenty-formula. A balanced remnant is conceded again (3:113; 3:199; 4:162; 5:66). QI-0003 / QCA-0004: the prior books are still something that can be upheld, not ash.
This sits one packet after 5:44–47’s “judge by the Torah / judge by the Injīl.” Upholding and judging-by are the same file.

packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP06 vv067-086
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP06
Unit: 5:67–86 (20 verses)
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

O messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. If you do not, you have not conveyed His message. God will protect you from the people. God does not guide the kāfir people. Say: People of the Book, you have nothing until you uphold the Torah and the Injīl and what was sent down to you from your Lord. What was sent down to you from your Lord will increase many of them in rebellion and kufr. Do not grieve over the kāfir people. Those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Ṣābiʾūn, and the Christians — whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does ṣāliḥ — no fear on them and they shall not grieve. We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent messengers to them. Whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a party they called liars and a party they killed. They thought there would be no fitnah; they were blind and deaf. Then God turned to them; then many of them were blind and deaf. God is seeing of what they do. Those who say God is the Messiah son of Mary have certainly disbelieved. The Messiah said: O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord. Whoever associates with God, God has forbidden him the Garden; his refuge is the Fire. Those who say God is a third of three have disbelieved. There is no god but one God. If they do not desist from what they say, those of them who disbelieve will be touched by a painful punishment. Will they not turn to God and ask His forgiveness? God is forgiving, merciful. The Messiah son of Mary is only a messenger; messengers have passed before him; his mother was a ṣiddīqa; they both ate food. Look how We make the signs clear for them; look how they are turned. Say: do you worship besides God what has no power to harm or benefit you? God — He is the Hearing, the Knowing. Say: People of the Book, do not go beyond bounds in your dīn other than the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who already went astray before and led many astray and strayed from the even way. Cursed were those who disbelieved of the Children of Israel on the tongue of David and of Jesus son of Mary. That was for their disobedience and their aggression. They did not forbid one another from munkar they committed. How evil is what they were doing. You see many of them taking those who disbelieve as allies. The self has sent ahead for them. God is angry with them; in the punishment they abide. If they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was sent down to him they would not have taken them as allies, but many of them are fāsiqūn. You will surely find the strongest of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say we are Christians. That is because among them are priests and monks and because they do not act proudly. When they hear what was sent down to the messenger you see their eyes overflow with tears from what they recognize of the truth. They say our Lord we have believed so write us with the witnesses. Why should we not believe in God and what has come to us of the truth, and we hope our Lord will admit us with the righteous people? So God has repaid them for what they said with Gardens under which rivers flow; they abide; that is the repayment of the good-doers. Those who disbelieved and called Our signs a lie — they are the companions of Jahīm.
2–3. Investigation
5:67–68 convey; you have nothing until you uphold

Convey what was sent down; if you do not, you have not conveyed the risāla. God protects you from the people. People of the Book: you have nothing until you uphold the Torah and the Injīl and what was sent down to you from your Lord. Same uphold-triad as 5:66, now as a “you stand on nothing” sentence. Increase-in-kufr refrain repeats 5:64.
5:69 the 2:62 formula again

Those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Ṣābiʾūn, and the Christians — whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does ṣāliḥ: no fear, no grief. Almost the same list as 2:62 (order of Ṣābiʾūn and Christians swapped). This is the third member of the QI-0004 cluster (2:62 / 3:19 / 3:85 / now 5:69), in a surah that also said today I perfected the dīn (5:3) and whoever seeks other than islām it will not be accepted (3:85). The packet records the recurrence. It does not close the file.
5:70–71 Israel’s messengers: some lied about, some killed

Covenant; messengers sent. When a messenger brought what their souls disliked: a party they denied, a party they killed. They thought no fitnah; blind and deaf; God turned; many again blind and deaf. Same kill-the-prophets file as 2:87 / 3:181 / 4:155.
5:72–77 God is the Messiah; third of three; they ate food

Those who say God is the Messiah son of Mary have disbelieved. The Messiah said: worship God, my Lord and your Lord. Associating: Garden forbidden; Fire. Those who say God is a third of three have disbelieved. No god but one. Desist; turn; He is forgiving. The Messiah is only a messenger; messengers passed before him; his mother a ṣiddīqa; they both ate food.

5:17–18 already named both slogans. 5:72 adds the Messiah’s own speech: my Lord and your Lord (echo of 3:51 / 19:36 / 43:64). Eating food remains the anti-divinity test. Do not go beyond bounds in the dīn other than the truth.
QB-0110 remains the contrast-ID. This packet adds the Messiah’s quoted worship-command as Level 1 speech attributed to him.
5:78–81 cursed on the tongue of David and Jesus

Those who disbelieved of Israel were cursed on the tongue of David and of Jesus son of Mary, for disobedience and aggression. They did not forbid one another from munkar. Many take the disbelievers as allies. If they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was sent down to him they would not have taken them as allies.

David’s curse-tongue is usually heard as the Psalms’ imprecations; Jesus’ as Gospel woes (Matt 23). POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP, not a verse-match. The charge is failure to forbid munkar plus taking kāfir allies.
5:82–86 nearest in affection: those who say we are Christians

You will find the strongest of people in ʿadāwa toward the believers to be the Jews and the associators. You will find the nearest of them in mawadda toward the believers to be those who say innā naṣārā. That is because among them are qissīsūn and ruhbān, and they do not act proudly. When they hear what was sent down to the messenger their eyes overflow from what they recognize of the truth. They say we have believed; write us with the witnesses. Why should we not believe in God and the truth that has come? We hope to be admitted with the righteous. Repaid with Gardens. Those who disbelieved and called the signs a lie: Jahīm.

This is the Quran’s warmest sentence about Christians as a named group. It sits in the same surah as 5:51 (do not take them as awliyāʾ) and 5:17 / 5:72 (God-is-the-Messiah is kufr). Hold all three. The warmth is tied to priests, monks, lack of pride, and tears at hearing this sending — i.e. to a recognizing remnant, not to a blank check on Christology.

QB-0122: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with the existence of a Christian recognizing-remnant (Acts’ God-fearers / later converts). CONTRAST with any reading that makes 5:82 cancel 5:72. Asbāb often name the Najrān deputation or the Negus. TRADITION for the names. Level 1 is the nearest-in-affection claim plus the priest-monk-no-pride reason plus the tear-scene.

packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP07 vv087-108
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP07
Unit: 5:87–108 (22 verses)
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

O believers, do not forbid the good things God made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Eat of what God has provided, lawful and good, and fear God. God will not take you to task for the laghw in your oaths, but for what you bind of oaths. Expiation: feeding ten poor of the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a neck; who does not find the means, fasting three days. Keep your oaths. O believers, wine and maysir and stones and divining arrows are rijs of Satan’s work; avoid them that you may prosper. Satan only wants to drop enmity and hatred among you in wine and maysir and to bar you from remembrance of God and from prayer. Will you not then desist? Obey God and obey the messenger and beware. If you turn away, know that Our messenger’s duty is only the clear delivery. On those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt there is no blame in what they have tasted, when they fear and believe and do ṣāliḥāt, then fear and believe, then fear and do good. God loves the good-doers. O believers, God will test you with something of the game your hands and spears reach, that God may know who fears Him unseen. Whoever transgresses after that has a painful punishment. O believers, do not kill game while you are ḥurum. Whoever of you kills it intentionally: an equivalent from livestock, judged by two just men among you, an offering reaching the Kaʿba; or kaffāra feeding poor, or the equivalent in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his affair. God has pardoned what is past; whoever repeats, God will take vengeance. Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, a provision for you and for the traveler; forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are ḥurum. God made the Kaʿba, the Sacred House, a standing for people, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands. That is so you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and the earth. Know that God is severe in penalty and that God is forgiving, merciful. The messenger’s duty is only the delivery. God knows what you reveal and what you hide. Say: the bad and the good are not equal, though the abundance of the bad amaze you. Fear God, people of understanding. O believers, do not ask about things that if they are shown to you will distress you. If you ask about them while the Quran is being sent down they will be shown to you. God has pardoned that. A people before you asked them, then became disbelievers in them. God has not made baḥīra or sāʾiba or waṣīla or ḥām. But those who disbelieve invent the lie against God, and most of them do not understand. When it is said to them come to what God sent down and to the messenger they say enough for us is what we found our fathers upon. Even if their fathers knew nothing and were not guided? O believers, on you are yourselves. The one who goes astray will not harm you when you are guided. To God is your return all together. O believers, testimony among you when death comes to one of you at the bequest: two just men from among you, or two others from other than you if you are traveling and the disaster of death strikes you. Detain them after the prayer; let them swear by God if you doubt: we will not sell it for a price even if he is a near kin, and we will not hide God’s testimony. If it is found that they merited a sin, two others stand, the nearest in claim, and swear: our testimony is truer than their testimony and we have not transgressed.
2–3. Investigation
5:87–89 do not forbid the good; oath-kaffāra

Do not make ḥarām the ṭayyibāt God made ḥalāl. Do not transgress. Eat the lawful good. Laghw of oaths is not taken to task; bound oaths are. Kaffāra menu: feed ten poor of family-average food, or clothe them, or free a neck; if no means, fast three days. Keep the oaths.

This is the brake against over-prohibition. It sits in a surah that just lengthened the food-ban list (5:3) and opened Book-people food (5:5). Both directions are in one book: do not eat X; do not invent new X.
5:90–93 wine path closes

Khamr, maysir, anṣāb, azlām: rijs of Satan’s work. Avoid them. Satan wants enmity and hatred through wine and maysir, and to bar you from dhikr and ṣalāh. Will you not desist? Obey God and the messenger. The messenger’s job is the clear delivery.

Wine path in this project: 2:219 (sin greater than benefit) → 4:43 (do not pray drunk) → 5:90 (avoid; Satan’s work). 5:90 is the closing avoid-command, grouped with gambling, stone-altars, and the same azlām already named fisq in 5:3.

5:93: no blame on those who believe and do ṣāliḥ in what they tasted, when they fear and believe and do ṣāliḥ — then fear and believe — then fear and do good. Traditional hearing: those who drank before the ban. Level 1 is a no-blame sentence conditioned on a three-beat taqwā-īmān-iḥsān.

QB-0129: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with wisdom-ban on drunkenness (Prov 20:1; 23:29–35) and with priestly sobriety (Lev 10:9). CONTRAST with Psalm-wine-as-gift and with John 2 / 1 Tim 5:23. NT has both warning (Eph 5:18) and use. This verse’s grouping of wine with lots and stone-altars is its own.
5:94–96 iḥrām game; sea vs land

A test with game the hands and spears reach, to know who fears Him unseen. Do not kill land-game while ḥurum. Intentional kill: equivalent livestock judged by two just men, offering reaching the Kaʿba; or feed poor; or fast the equivalent. Past pardoned; repeat: God takes vengeance. Sea-game and its food lawful for you and the traveler; land-game forbidden while ḥurum.
5:1–2 already banned hunt in iḥrām. This packet adds the kaffāra menu and the sea/land split.
5:97–100 Kaʿba a standing; messenger only delivers; bad is not good

God made the Kaʿba, the Sacred House, a qiyām for people, plus the sacred month, hady, garlands — so you know He knows heaven and earth. Messenger: only the delivery. Bad and good are not equal though the plenty of the bad amaze you.
5:101–105 do not ask; fathers’ custom; baḥīra unused; on you are yourselves

Do not ask things that if shown will distress you. If you ask while the Quran is coming down they will be shown. A people before you asked, then disbelieved in them. God did not make baḥīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla, or ḥām — four pre-Islamic livestock-taboo labels. Invented lie. When told come to what God sent down and to the messenger: enough for us is what we found our fathers upon. Even if the fathers knew nothing? O believers, on you are yourselves. The stray will not harm you when you are guided.
5:106–108 dying testimony

When death comes at the bequest: two just from among you, or two others from other than you if traveling. Detain after prayer; swear if doubted. If those two are found sinful, two nearer-claimants replace them and swear their testimony is truer.
A travel-exception lets outsiders witness a will. Later fiqh argues how far that goes. Level 1 is two-just, a substitute pair, prayer-timed oath, and a correction-oath.
QB-0130: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Torah two-or-three-witness rules (Deut 19:15) and with taking oaths in a sacred setting. The travel-outsider pair is this verse’s own.
4–9. IDs

Over-prohibition is banned in the same surah as the long food-list. Wine reaches its avoid-sentence. Iḥrām hunt gets a payment menu. Fathers’ livestock-taboos are named as invented. Next and last of this surah: 5:109–120 — God gathers the messengers; the table; did you say take me and my mother as two gods.

packets.title: S005 Al-Maida CP08 vv109-120
paragraphs: S005 — AL-MĀʾIDA — CP08  ·  SURAH CLOSE
Unit: 5:109–120 (12 verses)
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Overview

The day God gathers the messengers and says what response were you given? They say we have no knowledge; You are the Knower of the unseen. When God says O Jesus son of Mary, remember My favor on you and on your mother when I supported you with the holy spirit; you spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity; I taught you the Book and ḥikmah and the Torah and the Injīl; you designed from clay the likeness of a bird by My leave, breathed, and it became a bird by My leave; you healed the born-blind and the leper by My leave; you brought out the dead by My leave; I restrained Banī Isrāʾīl from you when you came to them with the bayyināt and those who disbelieved among them said this is only plain magic. When I revealed to the ḥawāriyyūn to believe in Me and in My messenger they said we believe; bear witness that we are muslims. When the ḥawāriyyūn said O Jesus son of Mary, is your Lord able to send down on us a māʾida from heaven? He said fear God if you are believers. They said we want to eat from it and our hearts be at rest and know you have told us truth and be among its witnesses. Jesus son of Mary said O God our Lord, send down on us a māʾida from heaven to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You; provide for us; You are the best of providers. God said I am sending it down to you; whoever of you disbelieves after, I will punish him with a punishment I have not punished anyone of the worlds. When God says O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people take me and my mother as two gods besides God? He says glory to You; it was not for me to say what I had no right to. If I had said it You would have known it. You know what is in myself; I do not know what is in Yourself; You are Knower of the unseen. I said to them only what You commanded me: worship God, my Lord and your Lord. I was a witness over them while I remained among them; when You tawaffaytanī You were the watcher over them; You are witness over everything. If You punish them they are Your servants; if You forgive them You are the Mighty, the Wise. God says this is a day the truthful will profit from their truthfulness; Gardens, abiding; God is pleased with them and they with Him. That is the great winning. To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and what is in them. He is powerful over everything.
2–3. Investigation
5:109 messengers gathered; we have no knowledge

All messengers are asked what response they received. They defer: we have no knowledge; You know the unseen. The courtroom is God’s; even messengers do not claim to know their communities’ hidden answer.
5:110 God recites Jesus’ file back to him

Favor on him and on his mother. Supported with the holy spirit. Spoke in the cradle and in maturity. Taught Book, ḥikmah, Torah, Injīl. Clay bird by leave; breath; bird by leave. Born-blind and leper by leave. Dead brought out by leave. Banī Isrāʾīl restrained when they said the signs were magic. Ḥawāriyyūn told to believe; they say we believe; witness we are muslims.

Every sign is twice-marked by leave. Cradle-speech is asserted here before Sūrat Maryam is reached. Magic-charge matches 5:110’s Israel-response. This is the longest in-Quran résumé of Jesus’ mission so far.
5:112–115 the table

The ḥawāriyyūn ask: is your Lord able to send down a māʾida from heaven? Jesus: fear God if you are believers. They want to eat, be reassured, know he told truth, be witnesses. He asks: a festival for first and last of us, a sign, provision. God: I am sending it; whoever disbelieves after, a punishment not used on anyone of the worlds.
The surah is named for this table. The Quran does not describe the food, the seating, or a last-supper plot. It is a requested sign-meal with a post-sign threat attached.

QB-0131: POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP with Gospel feeding-signs (Mark 6; 8; John 6) and with the Last Supper table (Mark 14 / 1 Cor 11). DIFFERENCE: no bread-as-body, no cup-as-blood, no Passover frame, no betrayal-at-table. John 6’s bread-from-heaven speech is the nearest thematic cousin and still not this scene. Do not baptize al-māʾida as the Eucharist.
5:116–118 the courtroom question

Did you say to the people: take me and my mother as two gods besides God? Jesus: glory to You; I had no right to say that; You would have known; You know what is in me; I do not know what is in You. I said only what You commanded: worship God, my Lord and your Lord. I was a witness while I remained among them; when You tawaffaytanī You were the watcher. If You punish them they are Your servants; if You forgive, You are mighty, wise.

This is the capstone of the negative Christology already mapped. The charge imagined is a two-god pair: Jesus and Mary. He denies having taught it. The refrain is the same: my Lord and your Lord. Tawaffaytanī returns (3:55; 4:157 file). He does not know what is in God. He leaves judgment to God.

Mary-as-goddess is not Nicene Christianity. The verse aims at a slogan the Quran treats as said. Whether that slogan maps to popular Marian devotion, to a polemic construct, or to a specific late-antique group is argued. Level 1 is the question plus the denial plus the worship-command he claims was his only message.

QB-0132 CONTRAST with any Christian confession that worships Jesus. PARTIAL AGREEMENT that Mary is not to be a goddess (the NT never makes her a deity; later popular devotion is a different file). The two-god pairing is this verse’s own targeting.
5:119–120 the truthful profit

This is a day the truthful profit from their ṣidq. Gardens, mutual pleasure between God and them. Kingdom of heavens and earth is His. He is powerful over everything. The surah that opened on contracts and a perfected dīn closes on a courtroom and a kingdom-sentence.
Surah 5 close-out

Al-Māʾida opened on ʿuqūd, perfected the dīn, opened Book-people food and marriage, restaged Israel’s land-refusal, told Adam’s two sons, set ḥirāba and theft, commanded judging by Torah and Injīl under a muhaymin Book, fenced walāya, called God-is-the-Messiah kufr, named Christians nearest in affection, closed the wine path, and ended with a table from heaven and Jesus denying a two-god teaching. Next canonical surah: S006 al-Anʿām.

pickthall.name: The Meaning of the Glorious Koran

verses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَوْفُوا۟ بِٱلْعُقُودِ ۚ أُحِلَّتْ لَكُم بَهِيمَةُ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَ مُحِلِّى ٱلصَّيْدِ وَأَنتُمْ حُرُمٌ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ
verses.itani: O you who believe! Fulfill your commitments. Livestock animals are permitted for you, except those specified to you; but not wild game while you are in pilgrim sanctity. God decrees whatever He wills.
verses.pickthall: O ye who believe! Fulfil your indentures. The beast of cattle is made lawful unto you (for food) except that which is announced unto you (herein), game being unlawful when ye are on the pilgrimage. Lo! Allah ordaineth that which pleaseth Him.

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تُحِلُّوا۟ شَعَٰٓئِرَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا ٱلشَّهْرَ ٱلْحَرَامَ وَلَا ٱلْهَدْىَ وَلَا ٱلْقَلَٰٓئِدَ وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًۭا مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَٰنًۭا ۚ وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَٱصْطَادُوا۟ ۚ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ أَن صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ أَن تَعْتَدُوا۟ ۘ وَتَعَاوَنُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلْبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ
verses.itani: O you who believe! Do not violate God’s sacraments, nor the Sacred Month, nor the offerings, nor the garlanded, nor those heading for the Sacred House seeking blessings from their Lord and approval. When you have left the pilgrim sanctity, you may hunt. And let not the hatred of people who barred you from the Sacred Mosque incite you to aggression. And cooperate with one another in virtuous conduct and conscience, and do not cooperate with one another in sin and hostility. And fear God. God is severe in punishment.
verses.pickthall: O ye who believe! Profane not Allah's monuments nor the Sacred Month nor the offerings nor the garlands, nor those repairing to the Sacred House, seeking the grace and pleasure of their Lord. But when ye have left the sacred territory, then go hunting (if ye will). And let not your hatred of a folk who (once) stopped your going to the inviolable place of worship seduce you to transgress; but help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty. Help not one another unto sin and transgression, but keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is severe in punishment.

verses.arabic: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ ٱلْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَٱلْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُوا۟ بِٱلْأَزْلَٰمِ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ ۗ ٱلْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَٱخْشَوْنِ ۚ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِى وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلْإِسْلَٰمَ دِينًۭا ۚ فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ فِى مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍۢ لِّإِثْمٍۢ ۙ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
verses.itani: Prohibited for you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and animals dedicated to other than God; also the flesh of animals strangled, killed violently, killed by a fall, gored to death, mangled by wild animals—except what you rescue, and animals sacrificed on altars; and the practice of drawing lots. For it is immoral. Today, those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them, but fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you, and have completed My favor upon you, and have approved Islam as a religion for you. But whoever is compelled by hunger, with no intent of wrongdoing—God is Forgiving and Merciful.
verses.pickthall: Forbidden unto you (for food) are carrion and blood and swineflesh, and that which hath been dedicated unto any other than Allah, and the strangled, and the dead through beating, and the dead through falling from a height, and that which hath been killed by (the goring of) horns, and the devoured of wild beasts, saving that which ye make lawful (by the death-stroke), and that which hath been immolated unto idols. And (forbidden is it) that ye swear by the divining arrows. This is an abomination. This day are those who disbelieve in despair of (ever harming) your religion; so fear them not, fear Me! This day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour unto you, and have chosen for you as religion al-Islam. Whoso is forced by hunger, not by will, to sin: (for him) lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

verses.arabic: يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ ۖ قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتُ ۙ وَمَا عَلَّمْتُم مِّنَ ٱلْجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ۖ فَكُلُوا۟ مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ
verses.itani: They ask you what is permitted for them. Say, “Permitted for you are all good things, including what trained dogs and falcons catch for you.” You train them according to what God has taught you. So eat from what they catch for you, and pronounce God’s name over it. And fear God. God is Swift in reckoning.
verses.pickthall: They ask thee (O Muhammad) what is made lawful for them. Say: (all) good things are made lawful for you. And those beasts and birds of prey which ye have trained as hounds are trained, ye teach them that which Allah taught you; so eat of that which they catch for you and mention Allah's name upon it, and observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is swift to take account.

verses.arabic: ٱلْيَوْمَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتُ ۖ وَطَعَامُ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ حِلٌّۭ لَّكُمْ وَطَعَامُكُمْ حِلٌّۭ لَّهُمْ ۖ وَٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ إِذَآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَ وَلَا مُتَّخِذِىٓ أَخْدَانٍۢ ۗ وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِٱلْإِيمَٰنِ فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُۥ وَهُوَ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ
verses.itani: Today all good things are made lawful for you. And the food of those given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. So are chaste believing women, and chaste women from the people who were given the Scripture before you, provided you give them their dowries, and take them in marriage, not in adultery, nor as mistresses. But whoever rejects faith, his work will be in vain, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
verses.pickthall: This day are (all) good things made lawful for you. The food of those who have received the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And so are the virtuous women of the believers and the virtuous women of those who received the Scripture before you (lawful for you) when ye give them their marriage portions and live with them in honour, not in fornication, nor taking them as secret concubines. Whoso denieth the faith, his work is vain and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter.

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ فَٱغْسِلُوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْمَرَافِقِ وَٱمْسَحُوا۟ بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْكَعْبَيْنِ ۚ وَإِن كُنتُمْ جُنُبًۭا فَٱطَّهَّرُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰٓ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌۭ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلْغَآئِطِ أَوْ لَٰمَسْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا۟ مَآءًۭ فَتَيَمَّمُوا۟ صَعِيدًۭا طَيِّبًۭا فَٱمْسَحُوا۟ بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُم مِّنْهُ ۚ مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍۢ وَلَٰكِن يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
verses.itani: O you who believe! When you rise to pray, wash your faces and your hands and arms to the elbows, and wipe your heads, and your feet to the ankles. If you had intercourse, then purify yourselves. If you are ill, or travelling, or one of you returns from the toilet, or you had contact with women, and could not find water, then use some clean sand and wipe your faces and hands with it. God does not intend to burden you, but He intends to purify you, and to complete His blessing upon you, that you may be thankful.
verses.pickthall: O ye who believe! When ye rise up for prayer, wash you faces, and your hands up to the elbows, and lightly rub your heads and (wash) your feet up to the ankles. And if ye are unclean, purify yourselves. And if ye are sick or on a journey, or one of you cometh from the closet, or ye have had contact with women, and ye find not water, then go to clean, high ground and rub your faces and your hands with some of it. Allah would not place a burden on you, but He would purify you and would perfect His grace upon you, that ye may give thanks.

verses.arabic: وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثَٰقَهُ ٱلَّذِى وَاثَقَكُم بِهِۦٓ إِذْ قُلْتُمْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
verses.itani: And Remember God’s blessings upon you, and His covenant which He covenanted with you; when you said, “We hear and we obey.” And remain conscious of God, for God knows what the hearts contain.
verses.pickthall: Remember Allah's grace upon you and His covenant by which He bound you when ye said: We hear and we obey; And keep your duty to Allah. Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men).

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.itani: O you who believe! Be upright to God, witnessing with justice; and let not the hatred of a certain people prevent you from acting justly. Adhere to justice, for that is nearer to piety; and fear God. God is informed of what you do.
verses.pickthall: O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity, and let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly. Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty. Observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do.

verses.arabic: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ ۙ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌۭ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
verses.itani: God has promised those who believe and work righteousness: they will have forgiveness and a great reward.
verses.pickthall: Allah hath promised those who believe and do good works: Theirs will be forgiveness and immense reward.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
verses.itani: As for those who disbelieve and reject Our revelations—these are the inmates of Hell.
verses.pickthall: And they who disbelieve and deny Our revelations, such are rightful owners of hell.

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أَن يَبْسُطُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنكُمْ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.itani: O you who believe! Remember God's blessings upon you; when certain people intended to extend their hands against you, and He restrained their hands from you. So reverence God, and in God let the believers put their trust.
verses.pickthall: O ye who believe! Remember Allah's favour unto you, how a people were minded to stretch out their hands against you but He withheld their hands from you; and keep your duty to Allah. In Allah let believers put their trust.

verses.arabic: ۞ وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَبَعَثْنَا مِنْهُمُ ٱثْنَىْ عَشَرَ نَقِيبًۭا ۖ وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّى مَعَكُمْ ۖ لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَيْتُمُ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَءَامَنتُم بِرُسُلِى وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ وَأَقْرَضْتُمُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا لَّأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّكُمْ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۚ فَمَن كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ مِنكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
verses.itani: God received a pledge from the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve chiefs. God said, “I am with you; if you perform the prayer, and pay the alms, and believe in My messengers and support them, and lend God a loan of righteousness; I will remit your sins, and admit you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever among you disbelieves afterwards has strayed from the right way.”
verses.pickthall: Allah made a covenant of old with the Children of Israel and We raised among them twelve chieftains, and Allah said: Lo! I am with you. If ye establish worship and pay the poor-due, and believe in My messengers and support them, and lend unto Allah a kindly loan, surely I shall remit your sins, and surely I shall bring you into Gardens underneath which rivers flow. Whoso among you disbelieveth after this will go astray from a plain road.

verses.arabic: فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَٰقَهُمْ لَعَنَّٰهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قَٰسِيَةًۭ ۖ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ ۙ وَنَسُوا۟ حَظًّۭا مِّمَّا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِهِۦ ۚ وَلَا تَزَالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَىٰ خَآئِنَةٍۢ مِّنْهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّنْهُمْ ۖ فَٱعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَٱصْفَحْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.itani: Because of their breaking their pledge, We cursed them, and made their hearts hard. They twist the words out of their context, and they disregarded some of what they were reminded of. You will always witness deceit from them, except for a few of them. But pardon them, and overlook. God loves the doers of good.
verses.pickthall: And because of their breaking their covenant, We have cursed them and made hard their hearts. They change words from their context and forget a part of that whereof they were admonished. Thou wilt not cease to discover treachery from all save a few of them. But bear with them and pardon them. Lo! Allah loveth the kindly.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا نَصَٰرَىٰٓ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَهُمْ فَنَسُوا۟ حَظًّۭا مِّمَّا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَأَغْرَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ ٱلْعَدَاوَةَ وَٱلْبَغْضَآءَ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۚ وَسَوْفَ يُنَبِّئُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَصْنَعُونَ
verses.itani: And from those who say, “We are Christians,” We received their pledge, but they neglected some of what they were reminded of. So We provoked enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection; God will then inform them of what they used to craft.
verses.pickthall: And with those who say: "Lo! we are Christians," We made a covenant, but they forgot a part of that whereof they were admonished. Therefor We have stirred up enmity and hatred among them till the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will inform them of their handiwork.

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيرًۭا مِّمَّا كُنتُمْ تُخْفُونَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَيَعْفُوا۟ عَن كَثِيرٍۢ ۚ قَدْ جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ نُورٌۭ وَكِتَٰبٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
verses.itani: O People of the Book! Our Messenger has come to you, clarifying for you much of what you kept hidden of the Book, and overlooking much. A light from God has come to you, and a clear Book.
verses.pickthall: O People of the Scripture! Now hath Our messenger come unto you, expounding unto you much of that which ye used to hide in the Scripture, and forgiving much. now hath come unto you light from Allah and plain Scripture,

verses.arabic: يَهْدِى بِهِ ٱللَّهُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضْوَٰنَهُۥ سُبُلَ ٱلسَّلَٰمِ وَيُخْرِجُهُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ بِإِذْنِهِۦ وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
verses.itani: God guides with it whoever follows His approval to the ways of peace, and He brings them out of darkness into light, by His permission, and He guides them in a straight path.
verses.pickthall: Whereby Allah guideth him who seeketh His good pleasure unto paths of peace. He bringeth them out of darkness unto light by His decree, and guideth them unto a straight path.

verses.arabic: لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ۚ قُلْ فَمَن يَمْلِكُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْـًٔا إِنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُهْلِكَ ٱلْمَسِيحَ ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُۥ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا ۗ وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۚ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
verses.itani: They disbelieve those who say, “God is the Christ, the son of Mary.” Say, “Who can prevent God, if He willed, from annihilating the Christ son of Mary, and his mother, and everyone on earth?” To God belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. He creates whatever He wills, and God has power over everything.
verses.pickthall: They indeed have disbelieved who say: Lo! Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary. Say: Who then can do aught against Allah, if He had willed to destroy the Messiah son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth? Allah's is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them. He createth what He will. And Allah is Able to do all things.

verses.arabic: وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ نَحْنُ أَبْنَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّٰٓؤُهُۥ ۚ قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُم ۖ بَلْ أَنتُم بَشَرٌۭ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ۚ يَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ وَإِلَيْهِ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
verses.itani: The Jews and the Christians say, “We are the children of God, and His beloved.” Say, “Why then does He punish you for your sins?” In fact, you are humans from among those He created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what lies between them, and to Him is the return.
verses.pickthall: The Jews and Christians say: We are sons of Allah and His loved ones. Say: Why then doth He chastise you for your sins? Nay, ye are but mortals of His creating. He forgiveth whom He will, and chastiseth whom He will. Allah's is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and unto Him is the journeying.

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلَىٰ فَتْرَةٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنۢ بَشِيرٍۢ وَلَا نَذِيرٍۢ ۖ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُم بَشِيرٌۭ وَنَذِيرٌۭ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
verses.itani: O People of the Book! Our Messenger has come to you, making things clear to you—after a cessation of messengers—so that you cannot say, “No preacher has come to us, and no warner.” In fact, a preacher has come to you, and a warner; and God is Capable of everything.
verses.pickthall: O People of the Scripture! Now hath Our messenger come unto you to make things plain unto you after an interval (of cessation) of the messengers, lest ye should say: There came not unto us a messenger of cheer nor any warner. Now hath a messenger of cheer and a warner come unto you. Allah is Able to do all things.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنۢبِيَآءَ وَجَعَلَكُم مُّلُوكًۭا وَءَاتَىٰكُم مَّا لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَدًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.itani: When Moses said to his people, “O my people, remember God’s blessings upon you, when He placed prophets among you, and made you kings, and gave you what He never gave any other people.”
verses.pickthall: And (remember) when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Remember Allah's favour unto you, how He placed among you prophets, and He made you kings, and gave you that (which) He gave not to any (other) of (His) creatures.

verses.arabic: يَٰقَوْمِ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْضَ ٱلْمُقَدَّسَةَ ٱلَّتِى كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلَا تَرْتَدُّوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَارِكُمْ فَتَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَٰسِرِينَ
verses.itani: “O my people, enter the Holy Land which God has assigned for you, and do not turn back, lest you return as losers.”
verses.pickthall: O my people! Go into the holy land which Allah hath ordained for you. Turn not in flight, for surely ye turn back as losers:

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوْمًۭا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَن نَّدْخُلَهَا حَتَّىٰ يَخْرُجُوا۟ مِنْهَا فَإِن يَخْرُجُوا۟ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّا دَٰخِلُونَ
verses.itani: They said, “O Moses, there are tyrannical people in it; we will not enter it until they leave it. If they leave it, we will be entering.”
verses.pickthall: They said: O Moses! Lo! a giant people (dwell) therein and lo! we go not in till they go forth from thence. When they go forth from thence, then we will enter (not till then).

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا ٱدْخُلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمْ غَٰلِبُونَ ۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓا۟ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
verses.itani: Two men of those who feared, but whom God had blessed, said, “Go at them by the gate; and when you have entered it, you will prevail. And put your trust in God, if you are believers.”
verses.pickthall: Then out spake two of those who feared (their Lord, men) unto whom Allah had been gracious: Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) if ye are indeed believers.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَن نَّدْخُلَهَآ أَبَدًۭا مَّا دَامُوا۟ فِيهَا ۖ فَٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ
verses.itani: They said, “O Moses, we will not enter it, ever, as long as they are in it. So go ahead, you and your Lord, and fight. We are staying right here.”
verses.pickthall: They said: O Moses! We will never enter (the land) while they are in it. So go thou and thy Lord and fight! We will sit here.

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لَآ أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِى وَأَخِى ۖ فَٱفْرُقْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
verses.itani: He said, “My Lord! I have control only over myself and my brother, so separate between us and between the wicked people.”
verses.pickthall: He said: My Lord! I have control of none but myself and my brother, so distinguish between us and the wrong-doing folk.

verses.arabic: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ۛ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةًۭ ۛ يَتِيهُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ فَلَا تَأْسَ عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
verses.itani: He said, “It is forbidden for them for forty years. They will wander aimlessly in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people.”
verses.pickthall: (Their Lord) said: For this the land will surely be forbidden them for forty years that they will wander in the earth, bewildered. So grieve not over the wrongdoing folk.

verses.arabic: ۞ وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ٱبْنَىْ ءَادَمَ بِٱلْحَقِّ إِذْ قَرَّبَا قُرْبَانًۭا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ ٱلْءَاخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
verses.itani: And relate to them the true story of Adam's two sons: when they offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them, but it was not accepted from the other. He Said, “I will kill you.” He Said, “God accepts only from the righteous.”
verses.pickthall: But recite unto them with truth the tale of the two sons of Adam, how they offered each a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the one of them and it was not accepted from the other. (The one) said: I will surely kill thee. (The other) answered: Allah accepteth only from those who ward off (evil).

verses.arabic: لَئِنۢ بَسَطتَ إِلَىَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِى مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ ۖ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.itani: “If you extend your hand to kill me, I will not extend my hand to kill you; for I fear God, Lord of the Worlds.”
verses.pickthall: Even if thou stretch out thy hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against thee to kill thee, lo! I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.

verses.arabic: إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثْمِى وَإِثْمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَٰبِ ٱلنَّارِ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.itani: “I would rather you bear my sin and your sin, and you become among the inmates of the Fire. Such is the reward for the evildoers.”
verses.pickthall: Lo! I would rather thou shouldst bear the punishment of the sin against me and thine own sin and become one of the owners of the fire. That is the reward of evil-doers.

verses.arabic: فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُۥ نَفْسُهُۥ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُۥ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ
verses.itani: Then His soul prompted him to kill his brother, so he killed him, and became one of the losers.
verses.pickthall: But (the other's) mind imposed on him the killing of his brother, so he slew him and became one of the losers.

verses.arabic: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًۭا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيُرِيَهُۥ كَيْفَ يُوَٰرِى سَوْءَةَ أَخِيهِ ۚ قَالَ يَٰوَيْلَتَىٰٓ أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَٰذَا ٱلْغُرَابِ فَأُوَٰرِىَ سَوْءَةَ أَخِى ۖ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰدِمِينَ
verses.itani: Then God sent a raven digging the ground, to show him how to cover his brother's corpse. He said, “Woe to me! I was unable to be like this raven, and bury my brother's corpse.” So he became full of regrets.
verses.pickthall: Then Allah sent a raven scratching up the ground, to show him how to hide his brother's naked corpse. He said: Woe unto me! Am I not able to be as this raven and so hide my brother's naked corpse? And he became repentant.

verses.arabic: مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًۢا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًۭا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحْيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًۭا ۚ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنْهُم بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ
